review:
I played this game in beta, on release, and to about 4 months after release
It was very good in the beta, we gave lots of feedback, spoke about the issues, etc
The devs listened to none of it. They then lied to us repeatedly. Then had the gall to fire the community manager who was actually communicating with the people and replace it with one of the previously mentioned incompetent devs.

The most suggested thing during the beta was matchmaking. Players who were level 50 could meet new players when they got out of rookie mode. On release this was not fixed, 3 months into release this was not fixed, by the time I quit the game there were so little players (about 200 a day from the original 12,000 on release) that matchmaking was basically impossible to fix.

Balancing suggestions were ignored and they buffed the things which were asked to be nerfed. This led to a downwards spiral of all the games being flooded with one class (the phantom), and the ranked gamemode dying. They added new mechanics such as rage which were not in the beta which vastly made classes (such as phantom) overly powerful while keeping classes which were weaker (such as marauder) in the dust.

Suggestions saying to fix bugs in beta were given. On release multiple of those same bugs existed. These include things such as daily quests being impossible to complete and various issues with optimization especially with the smoke ability

Suggestions regarding monetization, ignored. Before release they gave out a 60 dollar pack which contents were exclusive. They repeatedly promised us that it would be shut off after release. Release came and the pack was not shut off, they kept it open until a month after release. During that first month another three 60 dollar dlc packs were released. During this time they made no changes to balance, didn't fix various bugs, etc All a slap in the face to us as the game in that first month went from 12,000 players on release to a mere 2,000.

People cried out for the devs to stop this awful monetization strategy, they listened but also didn't. You see instead of making it just straight up money to buy you needed to buy gems to then buy the packs, which we got another 4 of all worth around 25-35 dollars.

The shareholders of this game are the Guillemot family of Ubisoft. The same family which repeatedly have screwed over game studios by making them change their games into cash grab pump and dumps via dlc, skins, and other content. 

Rattle, a fellow player during this time made a video explaining the problems faced during the time which explains it well. 
Here is the video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UMRGRhqidAk

This review doesn't mention everything awful that occurred here (examples including them firing community managers every 6 months or so) but there is more to explore if you were to go to the discord and ask the right people.

Do not play this game, do not support these people.

the game has unfortunately become a source of much turmoil within both the steam and discord chat boards.

the core idea and the art in this game is amazing. it had upwards of 25k at launch. it definitely got a lot of people's attention and for good reason. it was able to capture the fantasy of dragon airborne combat like no other game had done before it.

As time went on and they continued to refine the game they made some experience altering choices that changed the course of player engagement resulting in the game's average engagement being somewhere around 300-400 players.

 they limited playtime for ranked, would remove game modes, they cant decide whether or not to allow players to choose what few game modes they have still enabled and keep going back and forth between "you can pick" and "random mode chosen for you" 

they made one of the classes pay to play.

they charge upwards of 80 bucks for a 3 skin pack and call it "DLC"

instead of making match making skill based they simply chose to go into the game and disable the ability for players to view each other's levels in matches. 

they gave one class the god like ability to be BOTH  invisible, intangible, and a near one shot killer if you apply a lot of damage to that class. which makes you wonder how you're supposed to counter that mechanically within the confines and tools given within the game. especially when the full opposition all goes that one class. (Just run hide and pray you and your team aren't seen while they run down the clock)

they removed wall collision death for some reason making the fun (but delightfully tricky to aim) "force push" ability almost useless.

they keep giving us silver coins for completing daily missions but there's barely anything to use silver coins on in game. when they noticed that the majority of the community were sitting on hundreds of thousands of unused saved up silver coins (because as gamers, we love to complete our daily missions,challenges, and objectives) 
Instead of actually giving us stuff to buy in store with it (aka increasing the selection of non-gem based options in the store)
they charged hundreds of thousands for single dragon skin purchases.
No other options. Just a fast way to drain people's money to solve that problem
instead of making an actual variety of items you can purchase with the in game currency they put one or two items for insane amounts of silver to quickly drain your account. 

for the silver coin store they've still not included much other than a sword a helmet and some quotes. yes. quoted text that's only viewable if you make it top three at the end of a match or if someone views your in game profile

you cant really customize your rider. there's barely any drops. half the armor and swords are indistinguishable from each other unless youre REALLY scrutinizing the minor details. "this sword is curved near the handle slightly while that sword is completely straight" the capes look the same save for a fork tailed end or a clean cut tail. it's all the same fabric and material.

if you want to play to collect dragon eggs that would be cool but they dont really drop much. you can't get duplicates either so if you wanna choose between collecting all the eggs to have in your nest and view or riding the dragon into battle that's that. you'll never see that egg in the cool nest area again. or get to see that cute baby dragon animation loop. 

they say you'll get random dragon eggs when leveling up but it's untrue. you get one of two dragons like everyone else. we all got the same skins. and at level 60 (if i recall correctly) you get whatever in that PRE determined handful of skins you havent gotten already. there's no randomness to it. we all got the same things. 

there's already been dev confirmed on video proof of hackers using health regeneration. no known fix on that yet but it's slowly becoming more and more prevalent within the already unbalanced and small community 

They recently had an art competition and gave the winners 300 gems.
that's like 3 bucks.  not getting much other than a tag line there.

the leveling system in ranked acts so that you move up a milameter on the progression bar after winning 3 matches in a row but if you lose a single match you lose a whole level. I enjoy a good grind but this is unreasonable.

It's a weird spiral and things seemed to be great at the beginning but they keep making changes that make it harder to do anything with the game. they've almost entirely stripped the game of all player choice, customization, and progression.
what's left is being put behind pay-walls.

I write this review with a heavy heart but I believe people should read this before playing:
Century: Age of Ashes is a unique game centered around PvP aerial dogfights on dragons with 3 classes that all slightly but noticeably vary in play style. The game has a lot of potential and is amazingly fun with friends/ a party.
But having played from launch and participated in the events with a top 100 placing, over time I have begun to notice a lot of minor and major problems plaguing this otherwise very interesting game.
From horrid matchmaking where new players get matched against the top players, a store centered around overpriced reskins and recolours, the classes being unbalanced, game modes being removed for no particular reason, a band- aid approach to fixing the game from the developer, tone deaf towards the community, rewards being underwhelming for the time invested,  leveling being sluggish to the point of being annoying (as the developers had not added rewards past a certain level) and many other minor gripes...
I had a lot of fun with this game but I wouldn't currently recommend it to anyone.
If you play this game, don't buy anything. Money only gets you overpriced cosmetics. Play it for the fun experience and then either drop or continue with it but don't support Paywing any further, until they fix their major issues.

There is not much about Century: Age of the ashes that hasn't already been said.

Shortly; The game is a perfect example of F2P gone wrong, having lost over 90% of it's player base in the span of 7 months. Bells should have been sound that certain decisions made were the wrong ones to take.

Starting with the pre-order packs that were marketed as ''exclusive'' at a premium price, players including myself felt let down knowing their efforts were shamelessly blown away as soon as these items got available. 

As of first game modes were changed from a standard to a rotation, to the outcry of many players as they couldn't play their favourite game mode. 

Moving on, the game had a standard way of unlocking in-game cosmetics. IGC (In game currency) Or PGC (Premium game currency) And lets not forget about the season pass, though I find that more expectable

This, shared with the games additional cosmetic offerings as seen above, caused a strike yet again by the community as this time certain items were locked to buying a premium package that weren't offered in the games cosmetic store, unlike the pre-order packs.

Things only got worse, as eventually a 4th class was added, with additional skills for premium currency that quickly took the game out of balance, AGAIN to the communities displeasure. 

All this and more that I won't include due to this being long enough, caused the game to plummet. With gamers eventually stepping to something else, leaving a small community behind.

I still believe in this game. I adore the passion the devs have. But I really, really hope to see more positive changes, taken from the community. Balance the game, go a tad easier on cosmetics and this game will prosper.

I'm going to be extremely critical of this game and the developers behind it because I played the Beta for nearly 60 hours and was eagerly awaiting this game's launch, and have since completely lost interest because of some glaring problems with Playwing.

Like I said before, I played this game as much as I could during the beta and I loved it. To give credit where it's due, the core gameplay of Century is extremely compelling. The classes all feel great to play, the mobility is absolutely a high point of this game, and combat feels punchy and satisfying. I was eagerly awaiting this game's launch like a kid waiting for Christmas morning. The game launched and wasted no time in ruining the experience for me.

Constant server disconnects plagued the game at launch. Disconnects from matches which would negatively effect win/loss ratio, disconnects from the shop and menus, disconnects from the damn "Press a key to start" screen. The game was literally unplayable. Well, it seems to have been fixed for some players but here's the bad news. The game is STILL unplayable for many of us. To this day, I still deal with these constant disconnects that prevent me from even playing. I've tried a variety of troubleshooting steps, nothing has helped. If anything, as new patches came out, it actually got worse. My network isn't amazing, but it is far above the min requirement for the game, so this is completely unacceptable. 

Here's where it gets worse, Playwing has pretty much ZERO in the way of customer support and bug reporting. They run their reporting system primarily through discord, and it's a chaotic, disorganized mess where the bugs get buried and likely missed. This is appalling. Furthermore, the developers will not acknowledge the bugs or give any kind of indication as to whether or not they're being worked on. No status updates. Nothing. The discord is moderated terribly, with blatant favoritism towards top performing players. It's a joke. Playwing has recently added an extremely barebones, and seemingly non-functional bug report system through a site, but there's no email receipt that the issues have been received and they do not reply to these issues at all.

There is NO customer support. Furthermore, the monetization in this game is purely terrible. It's extremely aggressive and leans heavily into FOMO to get people to spend as much money as it takes not to miss out on this exclusive content that they'll be reminded of constantly via the game's bestiary. It's a completionist's/collector's nightmare. I'm pro monetizing via customization, battle passes, shop skins, etc - but the way Playwing has been doing this has indicated that they don't seem to know what they're doing and don't seem capable of learning from a constant barrage of rookie mistakes. They keep pissing the community off and rather than making an active effort to improve, they just apologize and repeat the same mistake time and time again. There's a ton of other shady practices, like allegedly letting the top leaderboard players from the beta continue to play and practice the game after beta ended for the sake of "player feedback". Balancing your game around the top players is usually fine, but not like this. If they needed more gameplay or class balancing feedback, they SHOULD'VE organized multiple public playtests or playtests that specifically target different player cohorts.

I don't want this game to fail and the studio to potentially face layoffs. Working in the games industry myself, studios shuttering or mass layoffs are everyone's nightmare. But I don't have high hopes for the longevity of this game. The game performed okay in terms of user stats at launch, but has been seeing a sharp decline since. This is a normal trend, launch weekend is typically the strongest for a game. That being said, the actual trend line is not normal. It's concerning. Keep in mind this game is still brand spanking new. 

Many players report that the matchmaking is straight up broken, but I wouldn't even know since I can't play the damn game since I get disconnected before even getting into a match. The way Playwing continues making the same mistakes, completely lacks any semblance of customer service/support, and just generally half-asses anything community related is ridiculous and something the studio should be ashamed of. They need fulltime, dedicated CMs and a pipeline for communication that allows players to actually feel as if they're being heard and acknowledged. AT LEAST for bugs and account issues, if not for everything else.

Don't get me wrong, running LiveOps on a live service game like this is hard BUT they're actively scaring players away. There's a lot of attention focused on events and whatnot to drive player retention, but even still their retention doesn't look too good from a high level because of a host of problems scaring the player base away. I'd like for them to turn this around, but I do not have high hopes. Can't recommend the game at this time, and unless they re-approach how to handle pretty much all communication with their players, I may never be able to recommend this game despite some amazing and fun gameplay.

Century: Age of Ashes is a fun and engaging experience with a unique game style. I played it at launch and have played most of my hours back then. After picking it up again and realising the same flaws continue to drag it down, I decided to write my review. I would recommend it if not for these issues:

The game is still trying to charge its players for game content beyond reason. The DLCs, the in-game store, practically all skins, and the new class are all STILL behind a paywall. This critique is coming from someone who is generally in favour of in-game stores who would not mind paying for appearances in games. 

The in-game currencies, gems and Iron Coins are obtained through either purchase or playing the game. While it looks like they have given players a more meaningful way to collect Iron Coins, it is still slow and penalized because the game itself is still bugged. This means you need to be prepared to have your time wasted. 

A personal experience with the queuing and matchmaking was getting thrown into a bugged infinite start-screen at the beginning of the match. Five other players and I got penalized for leaving early by alt-F4'ing to get out. Then again when I got thrown out of a match by losing connection to the game server despite having a stable internet connection. I lost any Scores, XP, and quests I might've progressed during that game.

I would ask you to reconsider before spending any money on this game and not to dump too many hours in it either. It's mostly just frustration playing since it was and is such a promising game that's being led in the wrong direction.

A free to play game where you get to ride a dragon in epic sky battles, what more to say ?!

Ah yes, the fact that it's visually beautiful and very well designed, the animations are smooth and the controls easy to pick up but tricky to truly master (movements and positioning are a core part of the gameplay), the maps are amazing to navigate and beautiful, the gameplay is very dynamic, fast paced and variable depending on the game modes and you can raise baby dragons ! The game also gives you a lot of quests to earn free content and is very generous with the offered content.

Now on the negatives, the choice of classes is still quite limited at the moment, but new classes will come ! The game also requires a decent PC to run, otherwise you might suffer some FPS issues, but it's also something that will get solved in the future. 
Some balance issues are quite frustrating but it's still a new game so balance issues are to be expected at this stage.
The impossibility to join back into a game when you have been disconnected even for a brief moment is a big issue tho, as well as dealing with leavers quite often with no compensation for their team, and I hope this will be fixed in the future. There's also zero way of communicating in game besides a few pings (there's no text chat and no voice chat), which can be very limiting for a team game, so I would recommend using Discord for coordination.

But overall, this is a great and fun game that will probably get even greater and even more fun as long as the devs keep their dedication to improve the game ! (which seems to be the case so far).

I do recommend this game but with some hesitations.

I have played since launch - great model design, fun fast paced gameplay and flying around on dragons is awesome.
There is new content added consistently - new dragons, classes, cosmetics, maps and modes.

That said, they have made some changes which unfortunately seem to be heading in the wrong direction.
First and foremost, they have clearly gotten greedy. The battle-pass has be reworked to give you essentially nothing unless you pay. Cosmetic packs are outrageously expensive for what they offer. You used to be able to earn in game currency, gems, just by playing. Collecting new dragons by hatching eggs used to be a core part of the game but I haven't seen an opportunity to get an egg for free since several updates ago. 

They changed it so any class can equip any dragon. Dragons are cosmetic so this is not game-breaking but it was entirely unnecessary and really takes away from the immersion. When there were three classes and three kinds of dragons each was matched to another and the abilities of each class made a lot more sense.

Cheaters. I suppose any game enough people play will attract cheaters after enough time but it really hurts this game. They are not in every match but when they are you might as well quit. You will be consistently one-shot out of nowhere and the game will not show you who killed you as it usually does. 

Overall flying on dragons is a blast and definitely worth trying out for free. Honestly, the mode where you just fly around a map by yourself is a highlight of this game. I still have high hopes for this game, they just need to better address the cheaters and pull way the fk back on the over-monetization.

Oh well... The pros and cons as I do now:

[h3]Pros[/h3]
 • Combats are active, you always need to be wary of your surrounding, and hope to escape if someone's hunting you from behind!
 • Graphisme is good, and you really feel the flight with the dynamic wind sound depending on your speed and direction.
 • 5 classes with different styles of gameplay.
 • Mastering your flight isn't easy, you will need to manage your stamina you can only refill at some points of the map.

[h3]Cons[/h3]
 • Sadly, the game is nearly abandonned. Season 3 is here since forever with no sign about when season 4 starts, if they planned one.
 • The dragon racing mode is really nice, but since it's not in the middle of a fight, the lack of music makes it feeling much less epic...
 • Matchmaking take quite a long time no matter the time of the day. It doesn't take 10 minutes, but you will rarely get to a game within 30 seconds. If the devs could work more on the game and attract more players, that could have been fixed.
 • The majority of cosmetic stuffs must be paid with real money to be obtained.

[h3]Subjective points[/h3]
 • No music during fights either, like for race, but since there are sound effects on death or kill, and the noises of fireballs and fire breath are frequent, I personally don't mind.
 • Controles won't be easy to Master, even if you have the Free Light mode to train or chill in the air.

[h3]Final note[/h3]
The game itself is good. And since it's free to play, you can give it a try and probably have fun from time to time. But don't expect any real new content in the future to keep you adicted to the game.

I loved this game upon first release. I missed the playtest, so I would spend hours watching recordings of those who got to play it with this itch in my brain that only playing this game would scratch. The gameplay is fast-paced, skill-intensive, and extremely fun. Upon first launch, items and cosmetics were attainable through playing the game, and I poured 106 hours into it. Character customization prompted meaningful emotional attachments to my account and how I played it, and the lore was intriguing and fun to immerse myself in.

Playwing, you have ruined my favourite video game with your poor management and greed.

You've taken the soul out of individual dragons by making repetitive reskins of legendary dragon skins and selling them for abysmal amounts each. It is highly appreciated that this game is not at all "pay-to-win," but $50 for a recolour is insane.

You've taken the soul out of individual species by for some reason removing the varying roars and sound effects of each species. I have genuinely considered creating dragon sound effects for each species and sending the files to whoever may be able to install them. This is a small issue that is extraordinarily frustrating because it really shows how downhill everything's gone because of your company's decisions.

Your company's lack of qualification to handle a game of this much promise is also shown in the quality of your updates/additions. Your animations have lessened in quality, the game is horribly optimized (I can't even play it on my perfectly fine gaming laptop because it lags out so hard on lowest graphics, I've had to get my fix through YouTube gameplay and even then it's still supremely dissatisfying). 

This decision was made a while ago, but I'm still critical of it: instead of adding new classes with their dedicated dragons, as would make sense with the established lore, you've chosen to allow different classes of rider to be mixed with different classes of dragon, then drop half-baked dragon species (also with no unique sound effects and crappy animations) into the game separately.

This game is and always will be one of my favourites out there. I am begging the company that owns it to either fix it or sell it to someone who can do better.

This game is all that I, as a big fan of dragons since childhood, have been wanting forever. Dragon flying and fighting with good graphics and an even better flight feeling?! I thought I'd never see it. The graphics and dragon skins are amazing, and the gameplay is challenging and asks a lot of practice and awareness. It gets my blood pumping every time, and I love this game so very dearly for its fluidity, its movement, and combat.

On the downside, the prices in the shop are almost atrocious, and make me wish the devs had put at least some kind of price tag on the game, so that I don't have to spend a fortune to make my dragons look as awesome as they can. I still pay for it with no regrets, but sure enough my wallet is crying.
On top of that, the devs can also be really deaf in terms of listening to their community, so I genuinely hope they work on that in the future- if there is one.

And a fair warning to new players: The (current) playerbase is very small, and a lot of people have been playing since launch or even beta. The learning curve is extremely steep, so I have to tell you that you WILL get dominated by other teams from time to time, unless you have a Veteran or two with you on your squad.
But trust me, it is so unbelievably fun once you get the hang of it.

100+ hours in Century: Age of Ashes and I can not recommend this game to anyone as of yet in it's current state. This game is unfortunately at an incredibly low player rate since launch. Starting at over 12k at early december and as of now (May 06) its barely at struggles to peak past 200 players. Until the game has resolved every issues it has maintained from launch and even to the issues it plagues today, There very little reason for newer player to play and stay and for veterans to return. 

Century: Age of Ashes have four game modes; Carnage (Team Deathmatch), Gates of Fire (Capture the Flag/Race), Skirmish (Smaller group Team Deathmatch) and Spoils of War (Gathering/Objective). Each game modes forces you to change your playstyle and has you playing in certain way to achieve victory for each one. With that being said, Ranked Matches only has one game mode, Spoils of War. To me, This is lacking for determining a players skill for each separate game mode. Especially when you gotta consider in some degree that Spoils is just gather as much as you can. While Carnage and GoF does have some form of teamwork/communication benefit that can help you achieve victory against a strong team. A player could be great at killing NPC's and bring home gold, But that doesn't mean they're a good player in dogfight or objectives. If the devs created a separate leaderboard/ranking system for each game mode, I would've been fine with that. Ah, Century - the game I had longed for for an ENTIRE YEAR together with one of my closest friends. When we first found the website and saw the first trailer, our minds were completely blown. The game was original, the different classes were noticeably different from each other, and the graphics looked heavenly. Plus, the game would be free - so we were really, really excited.

However, now that the game is out (and has been for a while now) - I can only really say that my impression of the game now, is a polar opposite impression than the impression I had of it when it was in early development. I can safely say that probably the entire community has the same opinion.. Well, if there even IS a loyal community that's left, lol. I don't know considering I see "I'm done with this game" messages EVERYWHERE in the official C:AOA Discord server.

When the game came out, the community was thrilled. The game was being praised for not being P2W, and the developers seemed to respond to their community well. The player-base was at an all-time high - peaking at about 12k players. At about the same time, there were news about an event coming out nearly instantly after release. Everyone was obviously excited for it - and so was I.

However, when the event launched, it was an utter mess. There were items made exclusively for the event (that were advertised in the event art and everything), but they weren't awarded through gameplay. Instead, a bunch of items compatible with only ONE class were awarded instead (and I can't say they were relatively pretty to be honest). I found it to be completely ridiculous. First, why not wait to have an event until you have cosmetics made for all classes? There were only three classes at launch, so it wouldn't even have been much extra work. Second, we expected to have cool dragons to work for through gameplay (that we had seen BEFORE the event launched, and expected to be the cosmetics we would be working for), but instead we got a bunch of random items thrown at us that were never shown anywhere before the event launched. Those dragons that were actually advertised in the event art? They were crazy expensive - only available to buy with gems (a currency in the game that is not awarded through gameplay, but instead awarded for every 5 levels you go up). It probably doesn't sound that bad, right? You work for the gems through levelling up, it makes sense. Well, no. Not in this case;

Keep in mind that at the time, you ONLY got 250 gems for every 5 levels (might've even been 150, I can't remember) - and the exp needed to level up, kept raising each time to ridiculous numbers. The dragons cost 2000 gems EACH. There were only three event dragons, but the only way to get them all would be to either pay the frick up and buy gems with real money, or sit inside 24/7, completely ignore the fact that you have a life and grind the heck out of every round to get those sweet, sweet gems. Also, it's important to mention that at the time, the classes were ridiculously imbalanced when it came to the different abilities, health and strength of each class - so there were a lot of opinions surrounding that too.
As expected, the community responded. Not with any hate, but with constructive criticism. We suggested that the devs would wait to make more cosmetics for each class next time, and that they needed to lower the prices of their cosmetics in general. We really thought they would listen, but lol no we sure jinxed it.

Everything went downhill from there. There have been many events - and none of them were really that great in any aspects. To be honest I got so pissed at the developers and the game in general that I left for about 4 months (I just recently returned and tried to give the game another chance) - so I'm only basing it on the opinions of the community and info from the game's wiki. Right now, the game has gotten a Fortnite-ish vibe to it - with seasons and exclusive passes??? Definitely proves that the developers are only in it for the money now. They really shouldn't have made the game free, because now they're throwing in DLCs worth nearly 300 dollars altogether because they're lacking money. It's okay for developers to make DLCs - there's literally nothing wrong with it. However, there was a case of them lying to the community when they added three DLCs that were only supposed to be available a few days after launch - kinda like a veteran player exclusive pack. For some reason though, they felt the need to let the DLCs be available a few more weeks without telling anyone. I was panicking to buy it in time, so I hate that they went "QUICK QUICK GET IT NOW" only to have it be availabIe for way longer, lmfao. I think that was the first time Playwing lost the trust of their community by lying - but it definitely wasn't going to be the last time.

Right now, the developers are like complete robots. They're unresponsive, they're being accused of firing community managers whom are the only ones that actually properly COMMUNICATE with the players, they've deleted the Discord feedback channel (I certainly couldn't find MY feedback message anywhere, lmao), they upload reskinned items from exclusive DLC packs and make them event prizes, they added a ridiculous "Rage Mode" (aka overpowered mode) that wasn't present in the beta and was only added right before launch without consulting with the community or anything, aaand they're slowly losing the trust of their entire community. FYI; in the first few weeks after launch, the player count dropped by 93%. I've NEVER seen a game perform so badly. Even games that are considered "dead", currently perform better than Century. Century is capped at a measly 150 players playing at a time, and that makes the matchmaking long and horrendous. Since I've tried to play a bit recently, I've only found myself getting through 10 rounds max in the span of 2-3 hours. That's AWFUL.

I've spent 60 bucks on the game, and oh how I wish I could get my money back right now. I don't think I'll return to the game at all now. The community is desperate and have started to aggressively swear at the devs (which honestly, I don't blame them for) - but are only met with robotic responses like "Please don't say that. Most of the devs don't even speak English." like.. UHM.. HELLO LMAO?!?!? PLAYWING, you have formed an entire loyal community that are DESPERATE to make this game work. They give you constructive criticism, and when you completely shut it out, they know that the only way you're going to respond to them is if they really push for it. Yet, when they do that, you only bother responding to their bad manners and not their constructive criticism. I'm so fricking done with these people. It's really sad. Finally, a game where you get to play the Dragon! Century: Age of Ashes is a PvP game where the player takes control of a Dragon and flies to fight other Dragon Riders into different game modes.

The game has been incredibly fun so far. Mechanically speaking, the controls are simple and extremely fluid, you simply fly the dragon constantly, boost for speed, break for a sharp turn, spit (?) fireballs towards your enemies, and finish them off with a good fire breath to turn them into ashes. I have been enjoying trying to lose my pursuer by trying to dodge their incoming attacks, quickly executing a sharp turn or squeezing through tight areas. On the other hand, the hunt is just as satisfying to try to keep up while trying to fight them. 

Graphically speaking, it’s quite beautiful, the level of details of your character and dragon is striking and the map is stunning. The music is also good and really adds to the overall atmosphere of the game. 

While there aren’t many different game modes, it is enough to keep you busy. The map is fun enough to navigate and the implementation of shield, health and speed boost are making the chase or your escape even more enjoyable. 
As such you can play in 6v6 games:
[list]
[*]Carnage: Team Death Match 
[*]Gates of Fire: Capture the Flag with some variations to it.
[*]Spoils of War: More original game mode that requires some PvE, PvP, escape and cooperation to successfully steal the enemy gold and secure it into your stash.
[*]Skirmish: 3v3 Arena PvP[/list]

All of these game modes are fast-paced, each game is quick. You can tell early on that while this game is easy enough to pick up, it is hard to master.

You will get to pick between three different classes. Each dragon-class share the common attacks explained above, but they all have their own special ability and ultimate along with a passive.

[b]Windguard[/b] is the support class. Their passive, Skeldan Resolve reduces shockwaves and negative effects on you. That class can also deploy a poisonous smokescreen to make you or your friends untargetable by the enemy while hurting them, the second option is a blast that can emit a shockwave. Their ultimate ability is Salvation Surge, she rushes towards an ally and offers healing and a shield boost.

[b]Marauder[/b] is a pure DPS class. Their passive is Relentless Predator that refreshes the cooldown on eliminations and assists. Their abilities are Frost Bolts and Gust, the first one does high shield damage while the second destroys incoming fireballs. Their ultimate ability Hunter’s Mark Marks an enemy and unleashes a flurry of fireballs should you manage to hit it.

Last but not least, the [b]Phantom[/b] class appears to be an assassin. Their passive is Guard shatterer that deals more damage to enemy shields. Their abilities are Mine and Blast. You can place a Mine for three minutes anywhere on the map and wait for a dragon to fly right into it. Blast launches a projectile that emits a shockwave. Their ultimate ability is Mystic shroud where they can become invisible and make a powerful fireball on their attack.

Dragons are highly customizable, through leveling and the shop. Some are pretty badass looking. The cash shop is not P2W (which was a question of mine considering the game is free). You also get dragon eggs that you can hatch by doing a few ‘quests.

On the downside, if someone logs out during the game, bug or rage quit, the game goes on with an unbalance of the sort. Absolutely not fun if you are on the receiving end. Furthermore, the matchmaking seems to be horrible but it’s fair to assume that it is still adjusting. It is only launch day after all! Though, the in-game menus are glitching and it’s proven to be a bunch of unnecessary game-reload if you want to play with your friends.

A little bit of story would have been amazing as I see some lore being integrated in the description of the regions and dragons. 

Finally, [b]Century: Age of Ashes[/b] is an extremely fun and FREE PvP game that finally allows you to be a killing flying dragon on your way to show your superiority on all the other Dragon Riders. With a great atmosphere and good mechanics, we can’t help but feeling that Playwing hit the spot.

I felt the need to update this review now years into the game's lifespan with no sign of improvement. 

As you might guess from over 1k hours of gameplay, I gave this game more than a fair go, I was actually a partner with them for some time, able to stream on their steam page and beyond. I took part in the betas before release, as well as a pre-release event before the game was actually finally released in the wild. 

TL;DR: I would not recommend getting into this game to... anybody. There's several reasons, I'll bring them down as follows for those that actually want to read a review: 

The good: 
- Beautiful graphics and gorgeous artwork. (Seriously the art team knocks it out of the park.)
- Fun PvP concept. 
- Dragons! (We don't have enough cool dragon-riding games) 
- Decent customization. 

The bad: 
- All of the gameplay.  
- Exorbitantly expensive premium shop.
- P2W abilities (that can be earned in game only after an eternity of grinding)
- Prohibitive battlepass system
- Disorganized development team with an us vs them mentality towards their playerbase and frequent turnover.

My Personal History: 
- Former moderator of their discord. (Left due to terrible community management and lack of care to improve from both Playwing and moderators at the time.) 
- Former Top 10 Player in the game (doesn't matter much anymore, didn't matter back then either.)
- 1k Hours of Gameplay spanning from release in 2021 to fall 2023. 
- Former partner of their game streaming team. 

This game has made some heavy missteps in its development, frankly a case study on how not to manage a game. At the time of release, things were chaotic, people were optimistic, and the crowds were hungry. 12k Concurrent playercount was by all means a big success for an "indie" dev. While decline was expected, had they managed it well, they should have been able to maintain good momentum with their player base but: 
- The team released the game, then left for THREE WEEKS during the peak of the holidays while the game was still non-functional. Stating that a team was on standby to handle any critical issues (except they apparently weren't). The Store was stocked with pure premium currency items, and games were practically unplayable. 
- The community management team s eemed at times muzzled and at times simply unable to provide answers for no good reason other than an apparent lack of desire or ability to communicate. This contributed to previous community managers departing out of frustration. 
- The moderator team dealt with the community with a heavy hand, silencing criticism and often resorting to bans for first time and minor infractions. (leading to the great Bell War of 2021) 

By the time a month rolled around 12k Players had dropped down to 1.2k as a combination of network issues, lack of communication, and terrible balancing took their toll. One class dominated early meta: Phantom. Make no mistake, gameplay heavily favored the phantom's untargetable invisibility, extremely long rage power, and buggy mines. 

Instead of gradual balancing changes done in tweaks at the suggestions of the playerbase, this was largely ignored with the initial reasoning given often coming down to "We've been developing games for a combined 20 years, you've only been playing for a few hours we know better." 

There was essentially no quality management as far as feedback went. It was either all or nothing with the developers and then what was implemented was usually counter intuitive to what most people were requesting. As a result we saw the implementation of additional cosmetics/cosmetic features (like hatching eggs and raising baby wyverns) over the balancing of  PvP in general which needs more rapid iteration. 

The number of players continued to decline dramatically. Don't just take my word for it, you can likewise check the charts of this game's history. It has never recovered from these dramatic initial mistakes. 

The majority of the active playerbase warned:
- Rage system would destroy balance. (it did.)
- Premium store was too expensive. (It continues to be, and remains unobtainable due to lack of regional pricing adjustments.) 
- Founder Packs were misadvertised. (They were, offered after release and later on iterations on the models/patterns found within the pack released.) 
- Premium packs were too frequent and too expensive. (After Founder Packs were removed, Arisen Packs went up for the same price differences, and a very short lived 'Lone Roar Pack' featured for 80 USD until it was removed due to backlash.) 

All this and more was continually ignored, other very unpopular issues included: Lack of reward for playing, removal of gem rewards post Season 0 for leveling, the introduction of battle passes with Season 1 closely mimicking the model of a much more popular game (Rhymes with Fortnight if you know what I mean), events that only favored players that knew how to abuse already badly balanced classes, exploits, and game time with little rewards for those that at least played the event. 

There was also a focus on adding more game modes before class balance was sorted, while maps were slow to be updated or otherwise ignored. "Lore" was introduced with the battlepasses that was hastily written and poorly translated. The leaderboard was often dominated by groups early on but they tried everything else before introducing a solo/duo queue and by then the game had essentially already been limping on two broken legs. Balances were often wide ranging and overtuned, playing into one another in a negative feedback loop of granting major dominance from one class to another. The UI was updated into something much harder to read for a majority of the playerbase. The in-game match UI was also made unnecessarily difficult to read. Going from clear reticles with visible (albeit at times buggy) HP bars to awkward floating bars and a hazy generalized reticle. 

Accessibility is abysmal. Advanced video options were never added. The developer (Playwing) saw a slash in funding basically two months in and a huge turnover of staff including one of the original game designers and product leads. 

The community itself also became very cruel, not to mention dangerous for some individuals. The moderators were known (at the time that I was active) for being petty and vindictive, fighting amongst themselves and dealing heavy punishment to anyone who didn't sing Playwing's graces or just didn't sit right with them. As a moderator I had to fight numerous times to adjust punishment scales so that people weren't being thrown out for the most petty things. I also had to stop individuals from exercising personal vendettas against individuals otherwise unaware of issues. The community manager that came in during the tumultuous first year after the best one was fired also fed the flames. 

Patch notes were often very basic and uninformative, with more details added only after people begged and even then often missing the details that people later discovered in the game itself like balance tweaks, map adjustments and even movement effects/UI elements. 

Customer support was abysmal at best, with people waiting months for a resolution that could potentially never come. I myself had tickets that never were answered or effectively solved. 

Events continued to be pushed out, favored in frequency over working on the issues in the base game, some bugs which continue to persist today. There's too much history and too many issues for me to go through, but it all comes down to bad feedback weighting and implementation.

My recommendation? Find another game. I know that sucks to say but this game does not deserve your time or your money. Take it from someone who played it damn near obsessively for close to a year. It breaks my heart, but I don't see it surviving for much longer, or gaining much more than 100 concurrent players for the forseeable, necrotic future.
